original_question: Can one construct presentations of the virtual biquandle in which classical crossings carry the linear non-commutative representation and virtual crossings carry additional nontrivial structure?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 8 ("Virtual Biquandle"), p. 23: construct presentations of the virtual biquandle with a linear (non-commutative) representation at classical crossings and some interesting structure at virtual crossings.
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact Problem 8. It correctly identifies that the question is about constructing presentations of a virtual biquandle, that the classical crossings should use a linear non-commutative biquandle-type representation, and that the virtual crossings should carry additional structure rather than being ignored. It also stays on the paper's intended narrow target, instead of broadening to general virtual-link invariants.
missing_details: The draft does not state that the paper's biquandle presentations are generators-and-relations constructions: one generator for each edge of the diagram, with relations assigned at crossings.
The draft does not make explicit that the surrounding biquandle formalism in Section 3.2 is for oriented virtual knot/link diagrams, and that the desired construction should apply in that setting.

The draft does not say that, in the nearby context of Section 3.3.1, a virtual biquandle is meant to combine biquandle structure at classical crossings with virtual-quandle-type structure at virtual crossings.
The draft does not state the invariance requirement under the generalized Reidemeister moves, which is implicit in asking for a bona fide virtual biquandle presentation.

The paper does not fix a unique non-commutative coefficient ring for Problem 8. Nearby classical-crossing examples include the quaternionic biquandle on modules over the ring of integer quaternions, equivalently described by a linear biquandle matrix with a central variable t; the refined question should therefore avoid pretending that the paper specifies one mandatory coefficient ring.

The exact virtual-crossing operations are not specified in the paper: the phrase "some interesting structure at virtual crossings" is intentionally open-ended, so no unique operator definition can be imported from the paper.

Homogeneity, degree restrictions, nilpotency conditions, asymptotic quantifiers, and phrases such as "for all sufficiently large m" do not appear in this problem at all, so they should be marked as not applicable rather than invented.
refined_question: Can one explicitly construct, for oriented virtual knot and link diagrams, a generators-and-relations presentation of a virtual biquandle by assigning one generator to each edge, imposing at each classical crossing the relations of a linear biquandle over a non-commutative coefficient ring (in the sense of the non-commutative linear/quaternionic example discussed nearby), and imposing at each virtual crossing additional virtual-quandle-type operations, so that the resulting presented algebra is invariant under the generalized Reidemeister moves?
justification: The draft targets Section 7, Problem 8 almost verbatim. To make it stand-alone and paper-faithful, the refinement imports only the nearby context that the paper itself supplies: Section 3.2 explains what a biquandle presentation looks like (generators on edges, relations at crossings, invariance under generalized Reidemeister moves), Section 3.3 supplies the relevant linear and non-commutative classical-crossing models, and Section 3.3.1 explains that a virtual biquandle is intended to merge virtual-quandle structure at virtual crossings with biquandle structure at classical crossings. I did not broaden the problem to classification, multivariable generalizations, or other algebraic variants, and I did not add unsupported conditions on rings, operators, dimensions, or other hypotheses that the paper itself does not impose.
